proof_summary: Prime-adic valuation bounds—using Fermat to obtain factors from Mersenne terms indexed by multiples of \(q-1\) and Legendre’s formula for factorials—show that every odd proper prime divisor \(p\mid n\) divides \(a(n-1)\); this contradicts \(p\nmid2^{n-2}\), while the remaining composite case \(n=2^e\) is excluded by the exact calculation \(v_2(a(2^e-1))=e-1\). Once \(n\) is prime, if \(r=\operatorname{ord}_n(2)<n-1\), the factor \(2^r-1\) forces \(n\mid a(n-1)\) (as \(n\nmid(n-1)!\)), again forcing the impossible divisibility \(n\mid2^{n-2}\); hence \(r=n-1\).
